# Intake Brief: Improved money/reputation animation

**Work item:** MS-0MUYT57J80021CWW · `feature` · `medium`

## Headline

When coins and reputation pips fly to the HUD they currently land on
hard-coded coordinates (`gameW * 0.25 + 70` for coins, `gameW * 0.5` for
reputation at `hudY`) instead of the actual on-screen position of the
"Coins: N" / "Reputation: N" numbers. The flights must end at the location of
the painted coin/reputation number.

## Problem statement

The HUD strip renders `Coins: N` left-aligned at `hudLeft + 10` and
`Reputation: N` left-aligned at `favourBandRight + 40` (positions derived from
the SLL layout and viewport, not fixed fractions of the screen width). Every
market of the codebase that animates coins/reputation to the HUD instead targets
static hard-coded fractions of `gameW`, so the landing point only coincidentally
coincides with the counters — and drifts (most noticeably for reputation, whose
number sits near the right of a label that can be wider than the assumed
position) whenever `hudLeft`/`favourBandRight` or the number of digits change.
The animation reads as coins "missing" the counter.

## Users

- **Player.** When a turn ends and coins/reputation resolve, the flying
  visuals should land on the counter numbers so the income visibly accrues
  into the player's totals.

### Example user story

> As a player, when I end a turn and coins/reputation fly to the HUD, I want
> them to land exactly on the Coins/Reputation numbers so I can see the income
> arrive in my totals.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Accurate landing.** Every coin/reputation → HUD flight lands within a
   small tolerance (≤ 2px) of the on-screen centre of the corresponding
   numeric value — the coin number for coin flights, the reputation number for
   reputation pips — across the supported viewports and digit counts. This
   covers: end-of-turn income collection (`animateIncomeCollection` +
   `collectIncomeGrids`), the `upcoming` income phase (HUD coin/rep
   destinations), incident-reveal delta bubbles, and the sell refund coin fly.
2. **Single source of truth.** The HUD render publishes one live anchor for
   the coin number and one for the reputation number; all animators consume
   the published anchors. No `gameW * 0.25` / `gameW * 0.5` target literals
   remain in `src/scenes/MainStreetAnimator*`.
3. **Layout drift resilience.** Anchors are recomputed whenever the HUD is
   re-rendered (including viewport/window changes), so subsequent flights
   target the current number positions.
4. **Presentation-only.** The change never mutates game state, the turn
   transcript, or the deferred-mutation window; reduced-motion and
   replay/headless modes remain flight-free exactly as today. No change to
   flight pacing, staggered SFX, or the income-phase choreography.
5. **Tests + docs.** Unit tests assert flight destinations equal the published
   anchors (coin and reputation paths); a browser test asserts the published
   anchor matches the rendered number centre of `coinText`/`repText`. All
   related documentation is updated (including `docs/main-street/ux-visual-audio.md`
   and code comments). Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- Presentation-layer only (defensive `try/catch` style preserved — a failing
  animator must never stall the turn).
- Must not change phased income pacing (~11s collection) or the
  `incomeCollectionActive` / deferred-delta timing windows.
- Must not regress the HUD layout geometry guards
  (`hud-strip-layout`, `hud-market-geometry-guard` browser suites).

## Existing state

- `src/scenes/MainStreetRendererHud.ts` lays out `Coins: N` at `hudLeft + 10`
  and `Reputation: N` at `favourBandRight + 40`, computing
  `repX = repText.x + repText.width / 2` (centre of the whole label, not the
  number) and passing `coinX: hudLeft + 70` to `animateHudValueChanges`.
- Animators hard-code HUD destinations as fractions of `gameW`:
  - `MainStreetAnimatorIncome.ts` — `animateIncomeCollection` (`coinX =
    gameW * 0.25 + 70`, `repX = gameW * 0.5`), `runIncomePhase` `upcoming`
    (`hudCoin`/`hudRep`), `collectIncomeGrids` (`coinX = gameW * 0.25 + 70`).
  - `MainStreetAnimatorBoard.ts` — sell refund (`coinX = gameW * 0.25 + 70`).
  - `MainStreetAnimatorIncident.ts` — delta bubbles (`hudCoinX`/`hudRepX`).

## Desired change

- During HUD render, compute and publish the live coin-number and
  reputation-number anchor positions (numeric glyph centre, i.e. label
  origin + prefix width + number-width/2) — e.g. new fields on `SceneLayout`
  or transient scene fields set by `refreshHudStrip`.
- Replace the hard-coded flight destinations with the published anchors,
  falling back to the current approximate coordinate only when the anchor is
  not yet available (e.g. very first render).

## Key Files:

- `src/scenes/MainStreetRendererHud.ts` — compute + publish coin/reputation number anchors.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetConstants.ts` — extend `SceneLayout` (or add scene fields) for the anchors.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetAnimatorIncome.ts` — consume anchors in `animateIncomeCollection`, `runIncomePhase` (`upcoming`), `collectIncomeGrids`.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetAnimatorBoard.ts` — consume coin anchor for the sell refund flight.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetAnimatorIncident.ts` — consume anchors for incident delta bubbles.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetScene.ts` — anchor storage/reset lifecycle.
- `tests/main-street/income-collection-animator.test.ts`, `upcoming-flow-animation.test.ts`, `incident-reveal-animator.test.ts`, `sell-demolition-animator.test.ts`, `tests/main-street/hud-strip-layout.browser.test.ts` — destination assertions.
- `docs/main-street/ux-visual-audio.md` — document the anchor source of truth.

## Related work

- **MS-0MUYAESVU007X2U8** — "Coin and Reputation should count up/down"
  (in-progress, idea): end-of-turn reconciliation coins/rep fly to/from the
  HUD totals and the totals should count up/down as the animation plays.
  Complementary: that item animates the *numbers*; this item fixes where the
  flights *land*. Do not duplicate.
- **MS-0MTV9AS15004AC1E** — "Visual representation of reputation" (completed).
- **MS-0MUYGFWXK003QFYB** / **MS-0MUZ4WB290024ZGQ** — reputation income coin
  sources (pedestrian dissolve); origins only, destinations unchanged here.
- **CG-0MUA1UH3A008M4BS** — Upcoming/incident delta-flow routing (the
  `resolveDeltaFlow` destinations consumed by the upcoming + incident paths).

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption — scope:** "coins/reputation flying to the HUD" covers every
  flight path that ends at the HUD counters (income collection, Upcoming
  deltas, incident bubbles, sell refund). If the operator intended a narrower
  scope (e.g. income collection only), the ACs narrow accordingly.
- **Assumption — anchor:** "the location of the number" = the centre of the
  numeric portion of the HUD label, not the centre of the whole label.
- **Assumption — digit drift:** the anchor is captured at flight launch; a
  number that grows during a count-up animation is handled by the separate
  count-up/down work item (MS-0MUYAESVU007X2U8), not here.
- **Risk:** anchor absent on the very first render (`previousCoins === null`
  path) — mitigate with a conservative fallback to the current approximate
  coordinate.
- **Risk — scope creep:** do not fold number count-up/down animation,
  new SFX, or pacing changes into this item; record any such opportunities as
  linked work items instead.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: "Which flight paths are in scope?" — Answer (assumption, record by
  Map): all coin/reputation → HUD flights (income collection, Upcoming
  deltas, incident bubbles, sell refund). Source: work-item description
  wording "coins/reputation flying to the HUD"; repo inspection of all
  `gameW * 0.25 / 0.5` HUD destinations. OPEN QUESTION for the producer if a
  narrower scope is intended.
- Q: "What is 'the location of the coins/reputation number'?" — Answer
  (assumption, Map): the on-screen centre of the numeric value inside the
  `Coins: N` / `Reputation: N` label. Source: item wording; contrast with the
  current `repX` (whole-label centre) and `coinX` (`hudLeft + 70`).
- Q: "How should animators obtain the destination?" — Answer (assumption,
  Map): publish live anchors from the HUD render path; no duplicated
  hard-coded fractions. Source: outcome of duplicate-check + code inspection —
  the HUD already computes the real text positions.
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **MS-0MUWE6MSQ006DEZ4** – End-reason & player-state model (completed)
- **MS-0MUMP96XH002SJ89** – Named storylines, outcome feedback & continuity indicator (completed)
- **MS-0MUO7CPH3003TXFI** – Reduce time upcoming event is shown (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `core/docs/DEVELOPER.md` — matched: 2px, absent, acceptance, actual, add (+246 more)
- `docs/main-street/ux-visual-audio.md` — matched: 0mtv9as15004ac1e, 0mua1uh3a008m4bs, 0muygfwxk003qfyb, 0muz4wb290024zgq, 11s (+224 more)
- `core/AGENTS.md` — matched: absent, acceptance, actual, add, aligned (+208 more)

# Intake Brief — Spread tier reputation thresholds and cap tier unlocks to one per game

Work item: **MS-0MV88T4I6000HQZG** — "Spread tier reputation thresholds per Monte Carlo ranges and cap tier unlocks to one per game" (`feature`, priority `high`)

## Headline

Tier unlocks by reputation currently fire in bursts (a median Medium run clears the 400/800/1200/1600 rungs in one go), so the ladder reveals content without pacing. Re-derive the 12-tier reputation thresholds from the Monte-Carlo-measured reputation distribution (Medium, achievement-rate steps) and cap progression at **one tier unlock per run**.

## Problem statement

Reputation thresholds for the early tiers (T2–T5 = 400/800/1200/1600) sit far below typical end-of-run reputation: a median Medium run ends around 2,900 rep, so `updateCampaignAfterRun` unlocks **4–6 tiers in a single run** (400, 800, 1200, 1600, 2400 are all cleared, adding the challenge triggers). Multiple new card families appear at once, there is no sense of a hard-won milestone, and the remaining ladder (up to T12 = 8000) is far out of reach — an unsatisfying pacing cliff at both ends.

## Users

Main Street players engaging with the campaign meta-progression (unlock ladder). The reputation path is the primary unlock driver; the challenge path is an alternative trigger per PRD M2.

Example user stories:
- "As a returning player, I want each run to unlock at most one new tier so that unlocking a tier feels like a milestone rather than a content dump."
- "As a player climbing the ladder, I want thresholds spaced so that consecutive unlocks are genuinely earned across several runs."
- "As a challenge-focused player, I still want the challenge path to unlock tiers, but it must obey the same one-per-run pacing."

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Threshold spread (reputation path).** The 12-tier reputation thresholds are re-derived from a **fresh Medium Monte-Carlo run on current HEAD** (≥ 200 seeds, greedy strategy via `src/scripts/monte-carlo.ts`, `economyHistory` final reputation) to hit the target achievement shares — the % of Medium runs whose end-of-run reputation clears the tier: **T2 90%, T3 75%, T4 60%, T5 45%, T6 35%, T7 25%, T8 18%, T9 12%, T10 8%, T11 4%, T12 1%**. The derived thresholds are recorded with the MC evidence (percentile table, run counts). Exact values may be rounded to friendly numbers and document that rounding; monotonic increasing order is preserved. (Existing `results/level2-gate-before-*.json` are treated as stale — generated 2026-10-07, before later balance changes; a fresh run is required.)
2. **T12 / top tiers stay aspirational.** No threshold is artificially compressed into the observed rep range; T12 (and the top tiers) may sit above the observed maximum and remain primarily challenge-path / long-campaign reachable.
3. **One tier unlock per run.** `updateCampaignAfterRun` (in `src/MainStreetSaveLoad.ts`) unlocks **at most one** tier per completed run: the **lowest newly-eligible locked tier** (no skipping), regardless of whether eligibility came from the reputation path, the challenge path, or both.
4. **Challenge path preserved but capped.** All challenge-based unlock conditions remain unchanged and still work as an alternative trigger; the one-per-run cap applies to them identically.
5. **UI consistency.** Any surface showing a tier threshold or next-tier target (e.g. `findNextLockedTier`/`scoreNextTierLabel` in `src/scenes/MainStreetHudTooltips.ts`) reflects the new thresholds; no stale hard-coded figures remain in i18n/UI text.
6. **Tests.** `tests/main-street/meta-progression.test.ts` is updated: the existing "unlocks multiple tiers in a single high-reputation run" case becomes an assertion that exactly one (lowest) tier unlocks; new cases cover cap semantics (rep-only, challenge-only, both-triggers, next-run continuation, already-unlocked tiers, T12 aspirational). All existing tier/progression/save-load tests continue to pass.
7. **Evidence + docs.** The Monte-Carlo reputation-distribution evidence and the new threshold table are committed, and the relevant docs are updated: `docs/main-street/prd-milestone-2.md` (US-1/update notes + threshold calibration appendix), plus `content-design-and-progression.md` if it restates thresholds. CHANGELOG.md is **excluded** (ship skill manages it).
8. **Full project test suite passes** with the change (unit + unit-cli + smoke, per the test skill).

## Constraints

- **Calibration basis (Q2-A):** thresholds are calibrated on **Medium** difficulty only. Easy runs will generally unlock faster and Hard runs slower — accepted drift documented in the brief/PRD (one ladder cannot pace all three economies equally).
- **No skipping (Q1-A):** the one-per-run cap always unlocks the **lowest** newly-eligible locked tier; the ladder is never jumped.
- **Achievement-rate steps (Q3-B):** thresholds are not evenly spaced; they are placed to hit the pre-defined share steps above. Where the Medium distribution is clumpy (a 5% band between ~794 and ~2152 yields a large threshold gap; the ≥2000–4500 mass yields tight mid-ladder gaps), the shares are authoritative and thresholds follow the data.
- **Challenge conditions unchanged** — out of scope to redesign; only their interaction with the cap changes.
- `campaign.unlockedTiers` / `milestoneHistory` schema and save/load format unchanged (only the number of tiers appended per run changes).

## Existing state

- `src/MainStreetTiers.ts` — `TIER_CONFIG` holds the 12 thresholds: 0, 400, 800, 1200, 1600, 2400, 3200, 4000, 4800, 5600, 6400, 8000; card-to-tier mapping lives in `src/card-data.csv` (out of scope here).
- `src/MainStreetSaveLoad.ts` `updateCampaignAfterRun` — iterates all locked tiers; `if (reputationMet || challengeMet) campaign.unlockedTiers.push(...)` → multi-unlock per run.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetHudTooltips.ts` — `findNextLockedTier` shows `requires Rep ≥ <threshold>`.
- `tests/main-street/meta-progression.test.ts` — US-1 tests pin old thresholds (400→T2, etc.) and explicitly pin "unlocks multiple tiers in a single high-reputation run".
- `docs/main-street/prd-milestone-2.md` §2/§8 (US-1) and Appendix B — PRD originally specified multi-tier unlock and 5-tier thresholds; expanded to 12 tiers (CG-0MT3C744B009DS84).
- Existing MC evidence: `results/level2-gate-before-greedy-{easy,medium,hard}.json` (200 runs each, 2026-10-07). Medium: mean 2632, median 2896, p10 132, p25 794, p50 2900, p75 3752, p90 4712, max 6272.
- MC harness records per-turn `economyHistory` (incl. reputation) but **not** `challengesCompleted` per run — challenge-path shares are measured separately or estimated during implementation; the share table above is reputation-path.

## Desired change

1. Run a fresh Medium MC calibration pass on HEAD; extract the final-reputation distribution.
2. Compute thresholds from the share table (percentile lookup), round sensibly, keep monotonic.
3. Update `TIER_CONFIG` thresholds.
4. Add the one-per-run cap (lowest eligible) to `updateCampaignAfterRun`.
5. Update the HUD-tier tooltip plumbing only if the new thresholds flow through configuration (no hard-coded UI strings).
6. Update tests + PRD/evidence docs.

## Key Files

- `src/MainStreetTiers.ts` — `TIER_CONFIG.reputationThreshold` values (primary change).
- `src/MainStreetSaveLoad.ts` — `updateCampaignAfterRun` one-per-run cap (primary change).
- `src/scripts/monte-carlo.ts` / `src/MainStreetMonteCarlo.ts` — fresh calibration evidence; note the harness currently omits per-run `challengesCompleted` (add if needed for challenge-path evidence).
- `results/main-street-monte-carlo*.json` — committed calibration evidence artifacts.
- `tests/main-street/meta-progression.test.ts` — cap + threshold tests.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetHudTooltips.ts` — verify next-tier threshold display uses `TIER_DEFINITIONS` (update if any stale constants remain).
- `docs/main-street/prd-milestone-2.md` — US-1/update notes, threshold calibration appendix.
- `docs/main-street/content-design-and-progression.md` — threshold restatements if any.
- `docs/dev/` / `CHANGELOG.md` — CHANGELOG excluded; no docs/dev change expected.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Clumpy MC distribution:** the Medium rep distribution is bimodal (a low cluster ~0–800 that includes collapsed/bankrupt runs and a dense 2000–4500 body). Percentile-derived mid-ladder thresholds will be close together (hundreds apart) on the dense body; the one-per-run cap is what prevents burst unlocks there, and the share steps are authoritative — exact value selection must be documented so the "too close together" complaint does not silently return.
- **Stale calibration source:** existing `results/` MC files predate later balance changes; thresholds are only finalised against a fresh run on HEAD. If the fresh distribution differs materially, the share table survives and threshold *values* follow the new percentiles (replan, do not fudge).
- **Challenge-path shares unknown:** the MC harness does not record per-run `challengesCompleted`; the share table above is reputation-path only. Adding challenge-path evidence is a possible small harness scope increase (note in plan, do not silently expand).
- **Save/load & schema:** only the number of tiers appended per run changes; `milestoneHistory` entries remain per-unlock (one per qualifying run). Existing saves with already-unlocked tiers must not regress (multi-tier saves keep their tiers).
- **UI text:** thresholds appear in HUD tooltip text — any hard-coded numbers must flow from `TIER_DEFINITIONS`; flag dead constants rather than silently updating strings in isolation.
- **Scope-creep guard:** redesigning challenge conditions, rebalancing rep sources, or adjusting card-to-tier assignments are explicitly out of scope; record such opportunities as linked work items, not gold-plating here.

## Related work

- **MS-0MUR9IMN60093HIE** (completed, high) — "Re-tune reputation sources…": ×4 retune of rep sources directly inflates the rep scale and makes the pre-retune thresholds (and any pre-retune calibration) stale.
- **MS-0MUXAL8HC005P9E4** (completed) — Level-2 gate MC evidence (`results/level2-gate-*.json`): source of the current (stale) reputation distribution.
- **MS-0MUQUBK1B006EODZ / MS-0MUQUBJ4J000IQT7** (completed) — Monte-Carlo baseline and evidence methodology this calibration extends.
- **MS-0MUR9I9WO004EW0M** (completed) — 5-turn payback rebalance; relevant economy vector.
- **MS-0MUYGFVIJ00070MB** (completed) — Reputation-phase invariant regression tests (guard against rep-path regressions while touching thresholds).
- Docs: `docs/main-street/prd-milestone-2.md` (M2 tier ladder, US-1, Appendix B), `docs/main-street/content-design-and-progression.md`, `docs/main-street/reputation-retune-evidence.md`.

## Appendix — Clarifying questions & answers (interview round)

- Q1 (round 1): "When a run would newly qualify for several locked tiers, which one unlocks?" — **Answer (operator): A — lowest newly-eligible tier (no skipping).** Source: interactive reply. Recommended option A chosen.
- Q2 (round 1): "Which difficulty should the threshold spread be calibrated to?" — **Answer (operator): A — Medium only** (Easy faster, Hard slower, accepted drift). Source: interactive reply. Recommended option A chosen.
- Q3 (round 1): "Preferred spread shape: evenly across p10–p90, or clustered to pre-defined achievement-rate steps?" — **Answer (operator): B — achievement-rate steps** (e.g. T2 by 80%, T3 by 50%…). Source: interactive reply. Recommended option A, operator overrode to B — brief follows B.
- Q4 (round 2): "Confirm the achievement-rate staircase (T2 90% … T12 1%)?" — **Answer (operator): "3. ?" — no preference / delegated to agent; proceeding with the recommended staircase** (90/75/60/45/35/25/18/12/8/4/1). Source: interactive reply ("?"). Interpretation recorded; revisit if the operator intended otherwise.
- Q5 (round 2): "May the top tiers (notably T12) stay aspirational above the observed rep max?" — **Answer (operator): "4. confirm / A" — yes, aspirational (option A)**. Source: interactive reply.

Research note: existing `results/` MC files predate later balance changes (running-costs etc.), so the brief requires a fresh calibration run; thresholds are targets, not final numbers, until that run lands. MC harness omits per-run challenge completion data — challenge-path share evidence may require a small harness addition (scoped at plan time).

Implemented display-only HUD reconciliation counting (MS-0MUYAESVU007X2U8).

Design (documented in code + docs/main-street/ux-visual-audio.md):
- New scene fields displayedCoins/displayedReputation — display-only running totals initialised to the pre-animation values when the deferred window opens (normal, non-reduced-motion, non-replay path only; the reduced-motion/tutorial/replay fallbacks are untouched).
- refreshHud() renders the running totals during the deferred window (falls back to previousCoins/state as before); animateHudValueChanges keeps receiving the pre-deferred values so sound/pop routing is unchanged.
- Steps: collectIncomeGrids counts up per collected grid icon (slot credited amount / icon count); flyCoinsToPoint/flyRepPips step up at a gain landing and down at a loss departure (signed displayDelta param); animateIncidentDeltaBubbles counts once per logical incident delta (capped bubbles share the signed total).
- Exactness: snapDisplayedTotals sets the totals to previous + pendingDelta at the collection finalize and the incident-reveal cleanup, so the final value lands exactly regardless of per-icon rounding or unanimated ongoing costs.
- Double-count guard: the incident delta is flown in the 'upcoming' phase AND re-enacted by the reveal; displayedIncomeCounted is set by the collection finalize so the reveal replay does not move the totals again.
- In-place text sync (syncHudTotals) so the on-screen totals visibly count without a full transient-clearing refresh.

Tests: new tests/main-street/hud-total-counting.test.ts (pure stepping + collection + upcoming flights + incident bubbles + reduced-motion exemption) and browser coverage added to main-street-renderer-deferred.browser.test.ts (mid-flight intermediate, in-place sync, final value, down-count).
